title: Refs KS-1931: a failed verification read stops the GDPR erasure cascade instead of continuing with an empty image list
body:
## Refs KS-1931: a failed verification read stops the GDPR erasure cascade instead of continuing with an empty image list

**TIER 1: product bytes change inside kyc, in the GDPR erasure path (personal data deletion); tier 1 by Wednesday's ruling for this row; the gate may raise it.** One product file changes, `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/src/index.ts` (+4 -2, three hunks), with one new test file (+151). One held Spark pass, raised unchanged as ONE pull request. Merge to develop only.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1931

## Summary

- **What changes.** `dbGetVerificationsByUser` caught every database or decrypt error, logged it and returned an empty list. `dbDeleteUserData`, the GDPR erasure cascade, collects legacy image ids through that helper and then deletes by `user_id` regardless, so on a failed read the cascade carried on with an empty image list. The helper now takes a second parameter, `throwOnError = false`; after its log line it runs `if (throwOnError) throw err;`, and the cascade passes `true` (`const verifications = await dbGetVerificationsByUser(userId, true);`). The cascade's own comment says failures THROW so the event bus retries and dead-letters; until now the read did not.
- **Behaviour change to read (statement 1; source: Wednesday's 14:45 wording).** A failed verification read now STOPS the erasure cascade. Before: it logged, went on with an empty image list and deleted the verification rows, so legacy images that only those rows pointed to survived while the route answered that all data was deleted. After pull request 1900, an unreadable thrown value took the same path; the new throw covers it too (cell R2). **Every other caller of `dbGetVerificationsByUser` keeps the empty list:** at develop `cea1cdc2b07d` the only other caller is the route that returns a user's verifications (`GET /api/kyc/user/:userId`, line 821), and cell C2 pins that it still answers an empty list. One nuance, from reading the code: the helper still returns an empty list when the database is not available (`if (!isDbAvailable()) return [];` before the try), unchanged, and the cascade itself returns 0 before it reaches the helper.
- **Unchanged by this PR (statement 2; source: Seat R 95th's gate-85 reading on pull request 1900, finding G85-F3, INFO, pre-existing).** The DELETE route (`app.delete('/api/kyc/user/:userId/data', ...)`, line 1223) still has no try block, so a failed cascade leaves that request unanswered; an unguarded DELETE rejection can exit the kyc process (a probe with a stand-in database, Express 4.22.3). Real database failure and a bus retry: UNMEASURED.
- **The test.** `ks1931-erasure-cascade-stops-when-the-verification-read-fails.test.ts` has 4 cells: two red cells (R1: an ordinary Error on the verification read stops the erasure before any DELETE and never answers 200; R2: the same for an unreadable thrown value) and two controls (C1: with the read working the erasure answers 200 and runs its three DELETE statements; C2: an ordinary read failure still lets `GET /api/kyc/user/:userId` answer an empty list). The harness is the ks1868 one: the real app on a real local listener with the database and subject-DEK modules replaced by stand-ins. Because the route has no try block, the cells give the request a short deadline and count the unhandled rejection themselves.
- **What it does NOT do.** It does not add a try block to the DELETE route, change the subscriber, the event bus or any retry setting, or touch any other caller. It says `Refs`: whether KS-1931 is finished is the board seat's call after the merge.
- **Held patch** (Spark pass, operator 135, 7,806 B canonical, sha256 prefix `60397c193e285f09` as measured by Seat R 109th; the READY states no hash for this format): the READY's fence equals its canonical patch and the two section files `cat` to it. Applied strictly at develop `cea1cdc2b07d`. The tree was built from the canonical patch; nothing in it was changed by Seat R 109th.

## Test plan / Test Evidence

**Touched:** two files, numstat equal to the held patch's: `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/src/index.ts` (4 added 2 removed) and `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/src/__tests__/ks1931-erasure-cascade-stops-when-the-verification-read-fails.test.ts` (new, 151 added). Base is develop `cea1cdc2b07d`, the same sha at plan time and at the push. The plan-time census (GraphQL, all pages, 101 open pull requests, 445 file rows) and the push gate's own read no open pull request on either path; the controls passed (a path of the newest open PR, 2210, hit exactly that PR; an absent path hit nothing). Develop did not move between the cut and the push.

**Host and runtime (stated per the repo's test-discipline skill).** Every run below was made on one Apple Silicon Mac (arm64), macOS 27.2.1, with no Docker stack started (the cells use stand-in database modules and a local loopback listener). Node is v26.8.1, the only Node on this machine; it is NOT the long-term-support line the repo's `CLAUDE.md` names (Node 24 today), nothing was run on Node 24, and the long-term-support status of Node 26 was not checked.

**Ran** (all by Seat R 109th, 2026-11-12, in tree `s-r109-ks1931`; evidence `evidence/row1931/`):
- **Strict apply:** `git apply --check -p1` rc 0 at develop `cea1cdc2b07d`, in a temp index at plan time (no offset line; controls: an altered context line read rc 1, a hunk header shifted by 3 read rc 0 with an offset line) and again in the tree; a doctored copy read rc 1; numstat of the applied tree equals the patch's (a planted difference read rc 1); changed lines per file equal (a planted difference read rc 1); the files changed in the tree are the two files in the patch.
- **Whole `services/kyc` suite on develop:** 16 files, 90 of 90 passed, rc 0 (load1 2.73 at the start, 1.67 s). The package's test script is a bare `vitest run`, so this is the script.
- **Whole suite after the patch:** 17 files, 94 of 94 passed, rc 0 (load1 6.08 at the start, 6.09 s).
- **Red first, then green:** with the product file put back to develop and the new test kept, 2 cells fail by assertion (R1 and R2: `expected [ …(3) ] to have a length of +0 but got 3`, the three DELETE statements ran) and 2 pass (C1 and C2); after the identical product diff was re-applied all 4 pass.
- **`tsc` with the test files** (a scratch config extending the service's own; the planted-error control fired, rc 2): rc 0, 0 error lines, 0 in the new test. Develop's own count with the test files was NOT run.
- **docs-fragments check, in my tree on the applied diff:** rc 0. No fragment is added by this PR.
- **`npm run audit:gate`** in my tree: OK (5 distinct advisories reported, 5 baselined).

**NOT run:** `eslint` (the kyc package has no lint script); a real database failure (the cells reject through stand-in modules); the DELETE route against a real database; the `user.erased` subscriber and a bus retry (not driven by these cells); the other packages' suites; the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6); any CI run (retired for this repo). The pre-push hook's legs (below) run the repo's checks on the pushed head.

**Docs fragments and changed-line comments (the repo's test-discipline skill).** NO-PAIR: this is a held local-model patch raised unchanged under the coordinating seat's no-pair ruling, so this PR adds no flow and cheat-sheet fragment pair. The patch itself adds a why-and-ticket comment line above the new throw, and the new test's header comment names the ticket and the reason. No line of the patch was edited. The gap is recorded for a follow-up across the held-patch pull requests of this lane.

**Migrations + config:** none.

**Pre-push hook:** (quoted from the push of this head by Seat R 109th)
```
PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.
  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.
  This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.
```
- Leg 14, verbatim: `shell suites: 127 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (of 127)`

## Before this deploys

- Nothing deploys from this PR. It reaches develop only; "deployed" reads as "on develop". The kyc service image would need a rebuild for the change to run anywhere, and the demo is frozen: none is granted by this PR.

## Notes for the gate

- **Provenance of the raise.** The patch is the Spark operator's held pass (operator 135); Seat R 109th applied it strictly, built nothing of its own, and pushed one commit.
- **The one behaviour change** is statement 1 above: a failed verification read now stops the cascade instead of continuing with an empty list. The DELETE route's missing try block (statement 2) is pre-existing and unchanged; with this PR a failed read now reaches it as a rejection where before the cascade would have carried on (by reading, not run against a real database).
- Branch name `feature/ks-1931-kyc-dbgetverificationsbyuser-returns-on-any` is Linear's own suggestion for the ticket; it carries no other ticket's key and no closing word.
